answer: I would anchor trust in Fishing boat skipper logbook with fisheries inspector stamp. With each logbook is seasons of recorded catches checked by a fisheries inspector, so a farm must sail a hundred real boats, a single tide check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the anchor of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The bridge is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
